hadith:
Holding Fast to the Qur'an and Sunnah - Narrated Abu Huraira:

The Prophet (ﷺ) said (to his companions), "Do not fast Al-Wisal." They said, "But you fast Al-Wisail." He said, "I am not like you, for at night my Lord feeds me and makes me drink." But the people did not give up Al-Wisal, so the Prophet (ﷺ) fasted Al-Wisal with them for two days or two nights, and then they saw the crescent whereupon the Prophet (ﷺ) said, "If the crescent had delayed, I would have continued fasting (because of you)," as if he wanted to vanquish them completely (because they had refused to give up Al Wisal).
message: Reflect upon the diversity of human nature; while some may harbor bitterness, others embody grace through humility and service. Remember that true strength lies in compassion and understanding, qualities exemplified by those who serve their communities without arrogance. Embrace these virtues to foster peace and unity in our interactions.
name:
Al Mubdi - الْمُبْدِئُ - The Originator

The name Al Mubdi represents Allah's attribute of being the Creator and the one who brings forth life and creation. It emphasizes the divine power to start all things and highlights the concept of renewal and new beginnings.
verse:
Al-Ma'idah - The Table Spread - 5:82

You will surely find the most bitter towards the believers to be the Jews and polytheists and the most gracious to be those who call themselves Christian. That is because there are priests and monks among them and because they are not arrogant.
